title: Multi-bit datasets with exactly two observed values are assessed as binary; the n×H_bitstring term of §3.1.3 is never computed
body:
## Summary

In `-i` (initial entropy) mode, every bitstring branch in `cpp/non_iid_main.cpp` is gated on `data.alph_size > 2` — the number of **distinct observed** symbol values (`cpp/shared/utils.h`, the `symbol_map_down_table` pass) — and the binary "Literal" Collision/Markov/Compression branches on `data.alph_size == 2`. SP 800-90B §3.1.3 makes the bitstring assessment depend on the **sample width** n: "If the sequential dataset is not binary … L samples (each having n bits) is considered as a bitstring of size nL … H_I = min(H_original, n × H_bitstring, H_submitter)".

So an n-bit dataset (n = 2..8, declared or inferred) in which exactly two values occur is relabelled to {0,1} (`utils.h`, "map down symbols") and assessed as a 1-bit source: the ten estimators run on the relabelled symbols, no bitstring is formed, and the n × H_bitstring term is dropped. Declaring the width explicitly does not change this. A comparator/threshold source captured into bytes (0x00/0xFF, 0x55/0xAA) is exactly this case.

## Reproduction

Built at `87c104d` (macOS, Apple clang + libomp; `selftest` agrees with `refdata` to 3.7e-10).

```
python3 -c "import random;r=random.Random(12345);b=[r.randrange(2) for _ in range(1000000)];open('twoval.bin','wb').write(bytes(2*x for x in b))"
./ea_non_iid -vv twoval.bin
#   Loaded 1000000 samples of 2 distinct 2-bit-wide symbols
#   H_original = 0.92162256445118362          (no Bitstring lines at all)
#   Assessed min entropy: 0.92162256445118362
./ea_non_iid -vv twoval.bin 8
#   Loaded 1000000 samples of 2 distinct 8-bit-wide symbols
#   Assessed min entropy: 0.92162256445118362  (declared width ignored)
./ea_non_iid -vv -c twoval.bin
#   H_bitstring = 0.089801499557893238
#   H_bitstring Per Symbol = 0.17960299911578648
```

Expected per §3.1.3 at width 2: H_I = min(0.9216, 2 × 0.0898) = **0.1796**. Actual: **0.9216** (5.1× higher). With the width declared as 8, the same battery on the 8L-bit string gives H_bitstring per symbol 0.3178, so H_I should be 0.3178; actual 0.9216. The same binary takes the bitstring path for the identical file in `-c` mode (gate `!initial_entropy`), which is how the missing term was measured.

## Direction

Reported figure too high whenever a multi-bit source happens to emit only two values; unbounded in principle (e.g. {0x00, 0xFF} at width 8).

## Suggested fix

Gate on `data.word_size > 1` / `data.word_size == 1` instead of `data.alph_size > 2` / `== 2`. Width-1 datasets and datasets with more than two values are unaffected (the two conditions coincide there); `selftest` refdata is unchanged by the change. Pull request to follow.

Found while auditing this tool for a downstream use that prices output length on the reported min-entropy figure.
